stories.title: Reuters reports a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, but confirmation remains limited
stories.summary: Reuters says The Wall Street Journal, citing US officials, reported a US strike on Qeshm Island after Iranian state media reported explosions. The island lies beside the Strait of Hormuz. US Central Command had not responded to Reuters at publication, and Washington had publicly signaled that negotiations remained possible. The operation's scale and consequences are not independently established.
stories.why: Qeshm's position near the Strait of Hormuz makes any escalation strategically sensitive for energy shipping, insurance and oil markets. Treat the strike as reported, not independently confirmed.

stories.title: US midterms begin with control of Congress at stake after Supreme Court rejects ballot challenge
stories.summary: Americans vote on November 3 in races that will determine control of the House and Senate, alongside governor, state and local contests. The Associated Press reports that the Supreme Court declined to intervene in the administration's bid to set aside roughly 20,000 California ballots flagged as potentially cast by noncitizens. California officials said the list contained errors and could disenfranchise eligible voters. Results were not available at briefing time.
stories.why: The outcome will shape the final two years of President Donald Trump's term, including the legislative path for budgets, trade and foreign policy. The ballot dispute also puts election administration and federal-state authority under scrutiny.

stories.title: Tesla and Samsung oppose possible new US tariffs on Vietnamese goods
stories.summary: Submissions to the US government show Tesla and Samsung opposing additional duties as a US investigation into Vietnam's intellectual-property practices approaches its November 29 deadline. Retail and consumer-goods groups also warn of supply-chain disruption, while US steel, seafood, plywood, solar and wood-product groups are pressing for penalties. Reuters reports that Vietnam's exports to the US rose 42% in the first eight months of 2026. Whether any new tariffs are proposed, and which sectors they would cover, remains unsettled.
stories.why: Vietnam is a major manufacturing and electronics hub for US-facing supply chains. New duties could affect exporters, foreign investment and prices, while the probe may also pressure Vietnam to strengthen IP enforcement.

stories.title: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals nearly $900 billion in computing commitments
stories.summary: An amended IPO filing shows Anthropic's third-quarter revenue reached $16.96 billion, up 47% from the prior quarter, down from 144% growth in Q2. The company disclosed $895.4 billion in future computing and infrastructure commitments with partners including Amazon and Google. It warned that some partners rely on third-party financing, so contracted capacity could be delayed, repriced, reduced or not delivered if funding becomes unavailable or more expensive. Anthropic also incurred $5 billion in additional compute costs during Q3.
stories.why: The figures expose the extraordinary capital and infrastructure required to scale frontier AI. Financing constraints could ripple through data-center construction, cloud providers, chip demand and investor expectations about AI profitability.

stories.title: NASA expects its Swift space telescope to re-enter Earth's atmosphere on November 4
stories.summary: NASA expects the roughly 3,200-pound Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory to re-enter on Wednesday, November 4, around 3:30 a.m. Eastern time, with an uncertainty of about 11 hours in the forecast issued November 2. Most of the spacecraft should burn up, although some fragments may survive. NASA says surviving debris is limited to a latitude band between 20.6 degrees south and 20.6 degrees north, and that harm to people is unlikely. The precise time and location remain uncertain.
stories.why: The possible re-entry corridor spans parts of Southeast Asia as well as large ocean areas, making this a timely example of the growing challenge of managing uncontrolled satellite returns. No specific impact point is predicted; NASA and the US Space Force are continuing to update the forecast.
